20. **Skills are the control surface.** Compose small markdown behaviors; share one to change many agents, remove one line to change one. `active-listener` lives in all 10 agents; `conversational-response` is deliberately withheld from workers so they stay verbose.

21. **The whole team is one YAML.** Add a team, prune a team, swap a member — one file, picked up on next launch. Colors, routing hints, roster. (But model/tools/skills/domain live in each agent's `.md`, not the config.)

22. **Config is where you scale horizontally.** The `plan-and-scale` preset runs *three parallel Engineering teams* from the same agent definitions — team count is a config knob.

23. **The model tier is a knob too.** Config `model:` overrides frontmatter `model:`. The `opensource` preset points 9 agents at 9 different providers — one interface, many brains.

## The mindset (spend, trust, scale)

24. **Spend to win.** "We are not afraid to spend to win here. We're not afraid to give our agents all the relevant context they need." 1M-token windows make deep specialization + memory viable — *if* you're willing to use the tokens.

25. **The $8 objection is a failure of imagination.** "You're thinking about right now. You're not thinking far enough into the future. Models will improve, costs are going down." The complaint dates you.

26. **You are not spending enough tokens.** Dan says it about himself too. The scarce resource isn't tokens — it's the willingness to reallocate work to compute.

27. **Where the ball is going, not where it is.** Build for the converging trends (rising intelligence, bigger context windows, cheaper tokens, customizable harnesses), not for today's constraints.

28. **2026 is trust and scale.** First raise trust until you *know* the team ships the result when you hit enter. Then scale — how big, how surgical. In that order.

29. **Systems that build systems.** The payoff of agentic coding: agents that plan, build, test, and validate your application so you compound your advantage instead of typing.

## Under the hood (for the "this is real" box)

30. **The nuclear UI pattern.** Three array assignments replace Pi's entire display layer while keeping the agent brain intact — the kind of hack only possible on a fully customizable harness.

31. **Every tier is the same binary, spawned as a subprocess.** `pi --mode json -p` with three extensions loaded; each self-exits unless its trigger env var is present. Elegant and uniform.

32. **Depth is capped by deleting an env var.** A lead strips `LEAD_MEMBERS_JSON` before spawning members, so the members' copy of the delegate tool self-disables. That's the whole recursion guard.

33. **The hardest problem is routing.** "Everything downstream only matters if the right team gets the right question." (OPUS.md) Teaching the orchestrator *when to delegate, what to delegate, and when to just answer* is the skill that compounds.

34. **The next frontier is parallel delegation.** `Promise.allSettled` already wraps the loop; the hard part is teaching the orchestrator when work is parallel-safe vs dependent. "Plan then build — sequential. Review from two angles — parallel."

35. **Track your spend or the footer lies.** The real `fix-worker-cost-tracking` bug: the TUI showed $8.79 while the API dashboard showed $34.28 — worker costs were silently dropped. Spend to win, *and* measure what you spend.

# Outdated vs Current — Multi-Team Agentic Coding / Lead Agents (`ma-2-lead-agents`)

What in this lesson is **period detail** (a specific tool/model/UI state at recording time) versus what is **timeless** (the tactic). Dan future-proofs the model/UI drift himself in-lesson — treat specifics as a snapshot, tactics as current. Written against the ecosystem as of **mid-2026**; the model-name and harness-capability axes move fast, so re-verify at publish.

Two kinds of drift are documented here:
- **A. Recording-vs-shipped drift** — where the video shows an *earlier* state than the checked-in repo (verified by reading both).
- **B. Ecosystem drift** — where the wider tooling has moved since recording.

---

## A. Recording-vs-shipped drift (verify against the shipped files, not the video)

### A1. The on-screen `orchestrator.md` predates the TillDone integration
- **In the video** (frame **t0768**), `orchestrator.md` shows `tools: read, grep, find, ls, delegate` and only **two** domain entries (`.pi/multi-team/`, `.`).
- **In the shipped file**, the orchestrator has `tools: write, edit, read, grep, find, ls, delegate, **tilldone**` and **three** domain entries (adds `.pi/multi-team/expertise/` with `upsert: true`).
- **Why:** `tilldone` was added *after* this recording — `specs/tilldone-multi-team-integration.md` is the plan that added it (orchestrator + the three leads gained the tool; workers deliberately did not). The video captures a mid-development state.
- **Teaching guidance:** teach from the **shipped** files. If you show frame t0768, caption it as "an earlier build — the shipped orchestrator also has `write/edit/tilldone` and can write its own expertise."

### A2. The front-end/back-end domain SPLIT is a live demo edit, not the shipped default
- **In the video** (frame **t1290**), Dan edits `frontend-dev.md` so its domain scopes writes to `apps/frontend/` (read+upsert+delete) while only **reading** the rest of `apps` — the "read the back-end, never touch it" rule — and shows the mirror-image edit for `backend-dev.md`.
- **In the shipped files**, `frontend-dev.md` and `backend-dev.md` have **identical** app-domain: `apps/` with read+upsert+delete. There is no `apps/frontend/` / `apps/backend/` split checked in.
- **Why:** the shipped repo is a "simple example" (a data-science, backend-focused target; Dan even notes the front-end dev isn't really needed for prompt-routing). The split is Dan demonstrating *what you would do* on a real front/back codebase.
- **Teaching guidance:** present the split as the *pattern to apply*, and be explicit that the shipped default is unsplit. Great "you try" lab step (see `lab-spec.md` S3).

### A3. The mental-model (expertise) files ship EMPTY
- **In the video**, the back-end dev's mental model is ~5,000 tokens of rich, structured notes (specs, missing infra, key risks, backend patterns, security, testing).
- **In the shipped repo**, all **10** expertise files are **0 lines** (verified with `wc -l`).
- **Why:** that on-screen model was Dan's *working copy from a previous codebase* — he says on camera, "I actually need to get rid of this and tune the mental model… it's got information stored about its previous codebase." `/install-into-codebase` creates **empty** expertise; agents grow their own per codebase.
- **Teaching guidance:** the compounding is the point, not the starter file. Weak students who open an empty file and think "it's broken" are missing that these are meant to fill in over sessions.

### A4. Dan's own description says "2 teams" — the shipped default is 3
- The video description says "9 specialized agents across 3 teams" in one place and "2 teams, 3 members each, 9 agents" in another.
- The shipped `multi-team-config.yaml` and the footer both show **3 teams / 10 agents** (1 orchestrator + 3 leads + 6 workers).
- **Teaching guidance:** use the code's numbers (3 teams, 10 agents). The "2 teams" line is a description inconsistency, not the system.

---

## B. Ecosystem drift (period detail vs timeless tactic)

### B1. Model names (`claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, "Haiku")
- **Period detail:** the agent frontmatter pins `anthropic/claude-opus-4-6` (orchestrator + leads) and `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6` (workers); the transcript names "Opus 4.6," "Sonnet 4.6," and "Claude Haiku." The `opensource` config names then-current third-party models (qwen3.5, kimi-k2.5, gemini-3-flash-preview, gpt-5.4/-mini, minimax-m2.7, mimo-v2-pro).
- **Timeless tactic:** **tier your models** — best intelligence where coordination happens (orchestrator + leads), cheaper where you just execute (workers) — or go all-Opus if you're maxing out. Dan blesses drift directly: models will improve; that's great; don't let it distract you.
- **Action at publish:** update model ids to the current tier equivalents; keep the tiering principle verbatim.

### B2. Sequential delegation only; parallel is the roadmap
- **Now:** the orchestrator delegates **one team at a time** (plan → engineer → validate). Dependent work is exactly right for this.
- **Coming:** `OPUS.md` names **parallel delegation** as the next direction — `Promise.allSettled` already wraps the delegation loop; the hard part is teaching the orchestrator *when* work is parallel-safe vs dependent ("review this PR" → Engineering + Validation at once). Independent cross-team requests are the near-term unlock, not the current default.
- **Teaching guidance:** tell the reader the ceiling is higher than what the video shows; don't imply parallel fan-out is already the behavior.

### B3. Two orchestration models coexist — don't conflate them
- **The Pi RUNTIME** (the lesson's subject) uses custom `delegate` / `tilldone` tools and spawns `pi` subprocesses. This is what runs when you type in the chat room.
- **The Claude Code BUILD harness**: the `.claude/` tooling — `plan-w-team.md`, `meta-pi-agent.md`, and the "Team Orchestration / Task*" sections of both specs — uses Claude Code's **Task\*** tools (`TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`Task`/`TaskOutput`) to *build and extend* the system. Claude Code is the **bootloader** (`/install`, `/install-into-codebase`).
- **Ecosystem drift:** Claude Code's own subagent/Task/background-task and Agent-Skills capabilities have grown since recording, which makes it *easier* to conflate the build harness with the runtime. Keep the two layers distinct in the chapter.

### B4. "Beyond Claude Code" — harness customization is less exotic now
- **The lesson's premise:** the Pi harness is customizable down to files/folders/tools/hooks/**UI** ("the nuclear UI pattern"), which is what lets Dan build a multi-team chat room. He notes you *can* build a more limited version in Claude Code via subagents + hooks ("Pi has the exact same system" of hooks).
- **Drift:** since recording, Claude Code and peers have expanded their own customization surfaces (Agent Skills with `SKILL.md`, hooks, output styles, plugins, settings layering). The **ideas** — teams, leads, domain locking, compounding memory, a single chat-room interface — now have more than one viable home.
- **Timeless tactic:** don't marry the tool. Dan: "More tools like this will emerge, but the ideas will be there." Anchor the chapter on the transferable architecture, not on Pi specifically.

### B5. Multi-agent tooling landscape
- The description name-drops **CMUX** alongside Claude Code as multi-agent tooling "here now." The specific tool roster will keep changing; the point ("multi-agent orchestration is the frontier right now, and the engineers who build these patterns get the asymmetric advantage") is durable.

---

## What is fully timeless (state these plainly)

- **One agent is a ceiling; teams of agent experts break it.**
- **Depth-2 delegation** (User → Orchestrator → Leads → Workers) with a **single orchestrator interface**.
- **Leads delegate, never execute**, enforced both softly (skill) and structurally (domain rules).
- **Domain ownership** (per-path read/upsert/delete) as the unlock for safe autonomy at scale.
- **Agent experts > generalists**, powered by **compounding, domain-scoped mental models** you let the agents self-maintain.
- **Composable skills** as the fleet-wide control surface.
- **Configuration-driven teams** — the whole roster in one file.
- **Model tiering + spend-to-win**, and the **2026 game of trust then scale.**

---

## Current-practice overlays (YouTube)

Both phase-1 overlays are sourced **directly from the lesson's own description** (real IDs, oembed-verify before publishing):
- **`f8cfH5XX-XU` — "Pi vs Claude Code"** → the named "beyond Claude Code / customizable harness / hooks" gap (Dan references it in-lesson).
- **`TqjmTZRL31E` — "CEO Agents"** → the immediately-prior lesson this one builds on (context / 1M window / multi-agent foundation).

See `extract.json` → `yt_overlay_candidates` for the full list and rationale (plus the phase-2 candidates).

# Lab — Multi-Team Agentic Coding / Lead Agents (`ma-2-lead-agents`)

**Goal:** operate, inspect, and reconfigure the multi-team system until you can explain the 3-tier architecture, domain locking, skills composition, and model tiering **without notes** — and prove each with evidence you produced.

## Scope contract (read first)
- **Course codebase only.** The shipped `lead-agents` repo **is the tool** (a Pi extension + `.pi/multi-team/` team definitions). The scikit-learn *prompt-routing classifier* codebase Dan operates on in the video is **NOT shipped** — so this lab runs the tool **against its own source repo** (exactly what `README.md` → "Step 2: Test Locally" prescribes). Do not try to reproduce the classifier benchmark.
- **No PiCanvas. No destructive Git/`rm` improvisation.** Restore any file you edit.
- **This costs tokens.** Even a light session can run several dollars. Have `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` funded or a Claude plan. Keep test prompts small.
- Every checkpoint below is **gradable** — it has an explicit, checkable pass condition.

---

## Setup

1. **Prereqs on PATH:** Claude Code (`claude`), Pi (`pi` or `ipi`), `bun`, `node`, `just`. Confirm: `claude --version`, `pi --version` (or `ipi --version`), `bun --version`, `just --version`.
2. **`.env`:** create `.env` from `.env.sample`; set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=...` (required). Optional provider keys only if you'll run the multi-provider config.
3. **Install:** from the repo root run `/install` inside Claude Code (or `just install`). It checks prereqs, verifies `.env`, runs `bun install`, validates the config + agent files, and adds a shell alias (default `teams`) to your profile. Reload your shell.
4. **Say the permissions out loud before launching:** open `.pi/multi-team/agents/orchestrator.md` and read its `domain:` block. What can the orchestrator read? What can it write? (Answer: read everything; write only its own expertise.)

---

## Checkpoint 0 — Launch + ping (the single interface)
- Run `just team` (default 3-team config against this repo). Wait for the chat room to boot.
- Type `ping`.
- **Pass:** only the **Orchestrator** responds (a pong-style message confirming Planning/Engineering/Validation are online), and the footer shows an Orchestrator line with cost + context tokens. You did **not** talk to any worker directly. *(Matches frame t0118.)*

## Checkpoint 1 — Three-tier delegation + a domain block
- Type: `ping each team lead`. Observe the two-layer fan-out (Orchestrator → 3 leads) and the footer summing lead costs.
- Then type: `have engineering present a tree structure of the most important files in this repo`.
- **Pass:** you observe the **Engineering Lead** attempt file access, get **domain-blocked** (visible ✗ / "restricted tool access as a lead"), and **delegate to a worker** (Backend/Frontend Dev) that actually reads the tree — three tiers in one exchange, results synthesized back up. *(Matches frame t0185.)*
- **Record:** one sentence — *why* did the lead delegate instead of reading the files itself?

## Checkpoint 2 — Reveal the full team (cost + model tiering)
- Type `/toggle-workers`.
- **Pass:** the footer/tree shows **all 10 agents** (Orch + 3 leads + 6 workers), each with its own **cost** and **model**; you can point to **Opus for orchestrator+leads** and **Sonnet for workers**. *(Matches frames t0232 / t1610.)*
- **Record:** the per-agent model tier and the total (orchestrator) cost at this moment.

## Checkpoint 3 — Multi-perspective (consistent fan-out)
- Ask a repo-relevant question of all teams, e.g.: `ask all teams: what is the single biggest risk in this codebase's architecture, and why?`
- **Pass:** the Orchestrator delegates the **same** (domain-tailored) question to all three teams and returns **one** synthesized answer noting consensus/splits — you never addressed a team directly. *(Matches frame t0408.)*

## Checkpoint 4 — Read the anatomy (where the config lives)
- Open and compare `orchestrator.md`, `planning-lead.md`, and `backend-dev.md` frontmatter, plus `.pi/multi-team/multi-team-config.yaml` and two skills (`zero-micro-management.md`, `active-listener.md`).
- **Pass:** you can answer, from the files:
  1. Which tier has `bash` and which does not? *(Workers do; leads/orchestrator don't.)*
  2. Where does an agent's **model / tools / skills / domain** live — the YAML or the agent `.md`? *(The agent `.md` frontmatter; the YAML holds only the roster + `consult-when`.)*
  3. Which skill is shared by **all 10** agents, and which is **withheld from workers** (and why)? *(Shared: `active-listener`. Withheld: `conversational-response` — workers stay verbose.)*

## Checkpoint 5 — Conversation awareness (the shared log)
- Find the current session's directory under `.pi/multi-team/sessions/<session-id>/` and open `conversation.jsonl`.
- **Pass:** you can see rows from **every tier** (user, orchestrator, leads, members) with `from`/`message`/`type`, proving every agent can load the shared conversation. *(Matches frame t1420.)*

---

## Stretch drills

### S1 — Prune a team (config-driven)
Kill the app. Either run `just team-pe` (Planning + Engineering preset) **or** copy `multi-team-config.yaml`, delete the Validation team block, and launch it with `just teamc <your-config>`. **Pass:** the relaunched roster shows **only** the remaining teams (no Validation lead/workers in the tree).

### S2 — Add a team (config-driven)
In a copy of the config, add a new team block (e.g. a "DevOps" team) pointing its lead/members at existing agent `.md` files (reuse engineering-lead + backend-dev is fine for the drill), give it a distinct color and `consult-when`. Launch with `just teamc <your-config>`. **Pass:** the Orchestrator lists/uses the new team when you ask something in its domain.

### S3 — Domain-lock experiment (the hard gate)
Edit `frontend-dev.md`'s `domain:` to scope writes to `apps/frontend/` only (read-only on the rest of `apps/`), mirroring the video (frame t1290). Relaunch, then via the Orchestrator ask Engineering to have the **Frontend Dev** write a file **outside** `apps/frontend/`. **Pass:** the `domain-enforcer` **blocks** the write (you see a refusal/blocked tool call), demonstrating the hard gate is structural, not prompt-only. **Restore** `frontend-dev.md` afterward.

### S4 — Model override precedence
Run `just team-oss` (multi-provider preset) **or** add a config-level `model:` to one agent in a config copy. **Pass:** that agent runs on the **overridden** model (visible in the tree), proving config `model:` beats the agent's frontmatter `model:`. *(Requires the relevant provider key in `.env` for `team-oss`.)*

### S5 — Read-only expertise
Add a second expertise entry to one worker with `updatable: false` (e.g. a "deploy-checklist.yaml" with a couple of lines) and reference it in `use-when`. Ask that agent to modify that file. **Pass:** the agent can **read** it but is **blocked from writing** it (read-only expertise is enforced by the enforcer's expertise check). Alternatively, observe `max-lines` enforcement by inspecting the `mental-model` skill's line-limit rule. Restore afterward.

### S6 — Scale horizontally (advanced)
Run `just team-scale` (Planning + **3 parallel Engineering teams**). **Pass:** the tree shows Engineering1/2/3, each with its own lead + FE + BE — team count is a config knob. (Watch the cost; keep the prompt trivial.)

### S7 — Meta build (advanced, optional)
Boot the meta agent with `just metacc` (Claude Code) or `just metapi` (Pi) and ask it to scaffold one new specialized agent + wire it into a config. **Pass:** a new agent `.md` + config entry that launches. *(This exercises the Claude Code build harness — distinct from the Pi runtime.)*

---

## Pass criteria (final sheet — all must be true)
1. The system is installed and launches (`just team` / your `teams` alias); `ping` returns an **Orchestrator-only** response with cost in the footer.
2. You **witnessed a lead get domain-blocked and delegate to a worker** (the three-tier cascade) and can explain why in one sentence.
3. `/toggle-workers` showed **all 10 agents** with per-agent cost and the **Opus-leads / Sonnet-workers** tiering; you recorded the tiers and total cost.
4. You **reconfigured the roster via YAML** (pruned S1 or added S2 a team) and relaunched successfully.
5. You **triggered a `domain-enforcer` block** (S3) by asking an agent to write outside its domain, then **restored** the file.
6. You opened `conversation.jsonl` and confirmed **every tier's** messages are logged.
7. Without notes you can state: the **3 tiers + what each may/may not do**; **where** model/tools/skills/domain live (agent frontmatter, not the config); the **soft vs hard** enforcement of "leads don't execute"; and **Dan's answer to the cost objection** (spend more; cost/intelligence trends favor you).

---

## Troubleshooting (keyed to the real mechanics)
| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| "Ghost" / duplicate messages when re-testing | Reused a live Pi/tmux session | Per `CLAUDE.md`: fully kill + recreate the session between runs; wait for the orchestrator to go idle before sending the next prompt. Prefer bun over npm. |
| Launch dies immediately | Missing `.env` or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `config.ts` `loadDotEnv` **throws** if `.env` is absent. Create it from `.env.sample` and set the key. |
| "FATAL"/crash naming an agent file | An agent `.md` referenced by the config is missing/renamed | `loadAgentConfig` throws on a missing agent file. Fix the path in your config or restore the `.md`. |
| A worker "refuses" / a write silently doesn't happen | The `domain-enforcer` blocked an out-of-domain tool call | Check that agent's `domain:` block. This is the feature (S3), not a bug. |
| Footer cost looks suspiciously low | Worker-cost propagation edge (see `specs/fix-worker-cost-tracking.md`) | Costs are captured across three layers; if a build predates that fix, worker costs can under-report (~25%). Cross-check against your API dashboard. |
| A lead tries to write code and stalls | Working as designed | Leads have no execution domain — they must `delegate`. This is the three-tier boundary. |
| Provider agent (team-oss) errors | Missing provider key | Add the relevant `OPENROUTER_/OPENAI_/GEMINI_` key to `.env`, or use the default Anthropic config. |
